comment: We came for three nights and stretched it in our heads for a week. The house was quiet after dark, and the kitchen had actually sharp knives.
Woke up to the smell of rain on stone. The host left a note about the bakery that opens at seven, and it was worth the walk.
Clean in the way that feels looked after, not staged. The bed was firm, the shower was hot, and the street noise died by ten.
Our kids spread out on the floor with the board games and we actually finished a conversation. That almost never happens on holiday.
The view is the one in the photos, which I did not expect. Evening light on the hills made the steep walk feel like part of the stay.
Check-in was a lockbox and a clear note. No waiting on a lane with our bags, which is all I want after a long train.
Coffee on the porch and no agenda. The neighborhood has a grocer a few minutes away, so we cooked two of the three nights.
Warm hosts, and they meant the recommendations. The dosa place they underlined was the best meal of the trip.
Space for four without anyone sleeping on a sofa. The extra blankets were in the cupboard, not something we had to request.
We worked one morning from the desk by the window. The wifi held a long call, then we closed the laptop and went to the water.
It smelled like soap and wood when we walked in. Floors were swept, towels were thick, and the hot water did not run out.
The pool was cool even at noon. We read, swam, and forgot to look at the clock until we were hungry.
A proper kitchen, not a kettle and a hope. We made pasta and ate it on the step while the lane got noisy and then quiet again.
The fireplace took a little patience and then did exactly what a mountain night needs. We slept with the window cracked.
Location is the whole point and it delivers. We walked to dinner and walked back without thinking about a cab.
Thoughtful touches: a clothesline, a torch by the door, salt already in the kitchen. Someone has stayed here and fixed what annoyed them.
The room was simple and that was right. We were out walking all day and only needed a good bed and a dark curtain.
The kids found the garden before we found the kettle. It is fenced, shady, and full of the quiet you do not get in the city.
Accurate photos, accurate description, and a better mattress than we had packed for.
We arrived late and the instructions still made sense when we were tired. Lights, lock, water. That was enough.
The terrace catches the breeze and almost none of the road. We ate breakfast out there both mornings.
It felt like a friend's place that happens to be beautiful. Nothing fussy, and everything was where you would look for it.
The neighborhood walks are the reason to book this over a hotel. We got lost on purpose and still found the river.
Heating worked on the one cold night, which was the night we needed it. The rest of the time we lived with the windows open.
Spacious bathroom, strong shower, and a mirror you can actually see in. A small thing, and a big difference with three people.
We celebrated a birthday here. The table fits six if you like each other, and we do.
Quiet enough to hear insects, close enough to buy fruit in the morning. That balance is hard, and this place has it.
The host answered a question about the trail in the house manual before we had to ask. We came back muddy and happy.
Design that does not get in the way. Good light, a real sofa, and somewhere to put a suitcase that is not the bed.
We will come back in the winter. The summer stay was already enough to plan around.
The beach was a short walk in shoes we did not mind getting sandy. There is an outdoor tap by the door, which tells you the host understands.
The cabin creaks in a friendly way. We played cards, burned one piece of toast, and called it a perfect evening.
A city apartment that still feels like a home. Blackout curtains, a serious coffee setup, and a supermarket downstairs.
Our parents are picky about cleanliness. They asked for the host's name so they could book it themselves.
Sunset from the roof was the photograph I did not know I was taking. The rest of the flat is calm and well kept.
Water pressure, wifi, and a mattress. They got the three things that ruin trips right.
We liked that the rules were few and specific. Shoes off, quiet after ten, enjoy the garden.
The treehouse is sturdy, not a gimmick. The ladder is fine if you take the bags up in two trips, which the note warns you about.
Lake light in the morning is almost unfair. We drank tea and delayed every plan we had made.
A comfortable base for a busy city. We dropped our bags and were on the street in minutes.
The pool is private enough that we swam before anyone else was awake. Coffee was waiting in the kitchen after.
Cool stone floors in the afternoon heat. We napped, which I think was the point of the booking.
The host met us with keys and a marked map. Useful, and not chatty in a way that trapped us in the doorway.
The bedroom faces away from the road. We slept through a festival we could still hear as a soft thump.
Exactly the kind of place you book when you want to cook one nice dinner and otherwise do nothing.
The views are wide and the glass is clean. That second part matters more than people admit.
We traveled with a toddler. Outlet covers, a stair gate, and a ground-floor bedroom saved the trip.
A generous checkout let us take the morning train without rushing a wet head. A small kindness, and we remembered it.
The estate around the house smells like rain and leaves. We did not turn the television on once.
I would send my closest friends here without a speech. It is comfortable, honest, and in the right place.
Lovely stay. The water heater needed five minutes to wake up, and after that everything was easy.
Great location and slightly firm pillows. We flipped one and slept fine.
Beautiful house. The wifi dipped once during a call, then recovered. Not a deal-breaker on a holiday.
We liked the neighborhood more than we expected and the sofa less. Still a solid few nights.
Clean and bright. The street is lively until about eleven, so light sleepers should take the inner room.
The kitchen is compact, but we managed a real breakfast. A larger pan would have helped, and we managed without one.
The photos are fair. The view is better in person, and the bathroom is smaller than it looks.
Warm host and clear instructions. We wished the desk chair was a little kinder on a long back.
The cabin is cozy for two and snug for four. We knew that, booked it anyway, and we were right to.
The pool was perfect. The walk up from parking is steep with groceries, which the listing does mention.
A good bed and a good shower. The living-room lamp was dim, so we read in the bedroom.
Check-in took a couple of messages to line up, then was smooth. The place itself was spotless.
We could hear a neighbor's music one evening. It ended, and the rest of the nights were quiet.
Charming and a bit idiosyncratic, in a way we grew to like by the second day.
The location earns the price. The interiors are simple and clean, which is what we wanted.
Heating took the chill off and did not quite make the room tropical. Bring a jumper for the sofa.
Breakfast was fresh fruit and eggs, unfussy and welcome. We still went out for coffee.
The view from the terrace is the reason to stay. The bedroom is comfortable and plain.
We enjoyed the walk to the water. The lane is dark at night, so the torch by the door earned its keep.
Nice flat, thin towels. Everything else felt considered.
The treehouse sways a little in the wind. I found it soothing. My sister did not. Worth knowing.
Great for a short city stop. A second mug would have made the morning less of a negotiation.
The house is beautiful in the late afternoon. Mornings are shady, which we liked once we expected it.
A solid stay with a kind host. The air conditioning in the bedroom is stronger than the one in the living room.
The place is fine and the location is better than fine. We had a slow drain on night two and a quick fix the next morning.
Comfortable enough for the price. The photos are a touch warmer than the rooms, and the bed was softer than we like.
We had a good trip overall. The check-in note missed a turn, so we called, and the host sorted it immediately.
A nice neighborhood and an ordinary interior. It was clean, though, and the kitchen did what we asked of it.
It rained the whole stay, which is nobody's fault. The roof was sound and the listed heater worked.
A decent base. We were out most of the day, and the bed and shower were good enough that we did not think about them.
